name: oreboot
why: coreboot rewritten in Rust, no C.
description: oreboot is a fork of coreboot, with C removed, written in Rust.

name: mu_basecore
why: Project Mu: Microsoft's maintained EDK-II fork, shipped on Surface and Hyper-V.

name: edk2-platforms
why: Board ports built on EDK-II; where platform-specific UEFI code lives.
description: EDK II sample platform branches and tags

name: opensbi
why: RISC-V SBI firmware, the M-mode stage that runs before the OS.
description: RISC-V Open Source Supervisor Binary Interface

name: u-root
why: Go userspace and bootloader for LinuxBoot; kexecs the target kernel.
description: A fully Go userland with Linux bootloaders! u-root can create a one-binary root file system (initramfs) containing a busybox-like set of tools written in Go.

name: petitboot
why: kexec-based OS bootloader used across OpenPOWER systems.

name: kexec-tools
why: Loads and boots a new kernel from a running one.
description: Kexec Tools: Userspace portion of Kexec

name: trusted-firmware-m
why: TF-M: secure boot and runtime for Armv8-M, the M-profile sibling of TF-A.

name: optiboot
why: The AVR bootloader shipped on most Arduino boards.
description: Small and Fast Bootloader for Arduino and other Atmel AVR chips

name: Adafruit_nRF52_Bootloader
why: UF2 and DFU bootloader for nRF52 boards.
description: USB-enabled bootloaders for the nRF52 BLE SoC chips

name: katapult
why: CAN, USB and UART bootloader for MCUs; common on 3D printer control boards.

name: tock-bootloader
why: Bootloader for the Tock embedded OS, written in Rust.
description: Software bootloader for boards running Tock.

name: STM32duino-bootloader
why: USB DFU bootloader for STM32F1 boards.
description: Bootloader for STM32F103 boards, for use with the Arduino_STM32 repo and the Arduino IDE

name: mbed-bootloader
why: Mbed OS bootloader with firmware update support.
description: Generic bootloader to be used in conjunction with Pelion Device Management Client

name: bootboot
why: Multi-architecture boot protocol and loader; sibling of EasyBoot, which is already in the corpus.

name: syslinux
why: SYSLINUX/ISOLINUX/PXELINUX. PXELINUX is named in the Type 2 keyword list but the corpus never contained it.
